# a11ign

> a11ign runs a real screen reader (NVDA) over web pages and reports the accessibility barriers a screen-reader user would hit, quoting the exact words it said. It is free, open source (AGPL-3.0-or-later) and sends nothing anywhere. It runs as a GitHub Action on a Windows machine GitHub provides, or from the command line.

Findings are evidence for a person to act on, not a score or a compliance certificate. A quick check that predicts what NVDA would say is coming soon and is always labelled a prediction.

## Start here

- [Test accessibility the way a screen-reader user hears it](https://www.a11ign.com/): a11ign runs a real screen reader (NVDA) over your pages and shows you the barriers it hits, with the exact words it said. Free and open source.
- [Get started with a11ign](https://www.a11ign.com/get-started): Add a11ign to your GitHub workflow, ask your AI agent to do it, or run it from the command line.
- [What a11ign checks and how it fits your tech stack](https://www.a11ign.com/what-it-checks): What a real screen reader catches that code checks miss, how a finding is decided, and how a11ign sits beside GitHub Actions, axe-core and your tests.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://www.a11ign.com/docs): Set up a11ign and decide whether to trust it: the GitHub Action guide, the evidence, security and how to contribute.
- [GitHub Action guide](https://www.a11ign.com/docs/github-action): The workflow file, the settings you will use, and what the GitHub Action gives back.
- [How we know a11ign works](https://www.a11ign.com/docs/how-we-know-it-works): How a11ign is tested, the numbers measured so far, and what is not proven yet.
- [Security](https://www.a11ign.com/docs/security): What a11ign does to a page, how to run it safely, and how to report a problem privately.
- [Contributing](https://www.a11ign.com/docs/contributing): Ways to help, how to run the checks, and the licence.
